item.description: - macOS: four tabs instead of six, shown as symbols beside the page's name. **Hotch** is home: usage, CPU, memory and thermals, a one-click Focus start and the last two clipboard items. **AI** puts each provider's plan windows above the sessions running on it. **Mac** is unchanged. **Desk** holds Focus, the clipboard and Backpack mode. - macOS: a Claude Code session shows the step it is on and how long that step has run, and a session waiting on you shows the command it wants approved. Codex sessions keep their project line. - macOS: an alert on the screen-edge tab is now a label beside the tab instead of a bar growing out of it, and the sessions ring turns amber while a session waits on you. - macOS: the screen-edge tab is one control. Hovering tints the whole tab and opens the card; a click keeps it open, also when it opened on hover, and a second click closes it without the hover reopening it. Its readouts no longer highlight or switch pages one by one, since the card's tabs do that. - macOS: the edge tab shows a usage ring for each AI provider, so Claude and Codex both appear, and Settings → Where Hotch lives chooses its readouts: Claude, Codex, Sessions, Memory and CPU, one slot each, and whether a running Focus timer takes the last slot. - macOS: switching tabs swaps the page in one frame while the card's height eases to fit. The page no longer blanks or cross-fades, the card no longer drops off its anchor when it grows, and clicking tabs quickly can no longer cut off the bottom of the card. - macOS: an available update is a green button at the bottom left of every tab. - macOS: Backpack mode lives on the Desk tab; the footer shows it only while it is on. - macOS: amber and clay status words are darker in light mode, so small text clears 4.5:1 contrast.

- macOS: Hotch now keeps itself up to date with Sparkle. Once a day it checks for a new version and shows the release notes with Install, Remind Me Later and Skip This Version. Check for Updates… is in Settings → App updates and the Hotch menu. - macOS: if you have Hotch 2.2.0 or 2.3.0, download this version from the release page once, as those versions cannot update themselves. Later versions arrive in the app. - macOS: an update window never appears over the welcome or during a Focus run. A line in the card says an update is available and brings the window back. - macOS: Download and install updates automatically is an opt-in in Settings. It waits until the card is closed and no Focus timer or Backpack session is running, or until you quit. - macOS: a Focus timer running when an update installs carries on in the new version. - macOS: the update check sends only the Hotch and Sparkle versions to hotch.hotherside.com and can be turned off. Sparkle's anonymous system profile is off. Sparkle is Hotch's first third-party package. - Linux: the GNOME top-bar button is back. 2.3.0 left it out of the panel, so the default top-bar home showed nothing and the card opened at the screen's left edge. Fixed by Simon (@sire6). - Linux: say when a newer Linux release is out, checking GitHub at most once a day and on demand (`hotch update-check`). A quiet line in the GNOME card footer and a tray menu item link to the release page, with **Skip this version**; Hotch never downloads or installs updates. Turn it off in Settings or with `hotch settings set updateChecks false`. Releases that change only macOS no longer attach Linux packages, so Linux users hear only about releases that change Linux. - Linux: **Check now** in Settings says when it could not check (offline, rate-limited, or no package for this machine). `hotch settings set updateSkipped` accepts `v2.4.0` as well as `2.4.0`.
